# File path built from HTTP request data (Go)

`qualor:go/path-traversal` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Data from the HTTP request that reaches the path of a file the server opens, creates, writes,
removes or serves: `os.Open`, `os.OpenFile`, `os.Create`, `os.ReadFile`, `os.WriteFile`,
`os.Remove`, `http.ServeFile`, and the file helpers of Gin and Echo, among others. Request data is
followed through `net/http`, Gin, Echo, chi and gorilla/mux, including JSON bodies.

Code inside a test (a function or method that takes a `*testing.T`, `*testing.B`, `*testing.F`,
`*testing.M` or `testing.TB`, such as the handler of an `httptest` server a test helper starts) is
not reported: it only serves the test's own requests.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
`filepath.Join("/srv/reports", name)` does not keep the result inside `/srv/reports`: a name of
`../../etc/passwd` walks out of it, and an absolute name replaces the base entirely in many APIs.
The client can then read configuration files and keys, overwrite files the server trusts, or
delete data.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the file name from the query string is joined to a directory and served.

```go
package reports

import (
	"net/http"
	"path/filepath"
)

func Download(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	name := r.URL.Query().Get("file")
	http.ServeFile(w, r, filepath.Join("/srv/reports", name))
}
```

**Compliant:** the file is opened through `os.OpenInRoot`, which refuses names that leave the
directory (Go 1.24).

```go
package reports

import (
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"os"
)

func Download(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	f, err := os.OpenInRoot("/srv/reports", r.URL.Query().Get("file"))
	if err != nil {
		http.NotFound(w, r)
		return
	}
	defer f.Close()
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
	io.Copy(w, f)
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Open the file through `os.OpenInRoot(dir, name)` or an `os.Root` (`os.OpenRoot(dir)`, then
  `root.Open(name)`), available since Go 1.24. They reject names that escape the directory,
  including through symbolic links.
- Or keep only the last element of the name with `filepath.Base` (and reject `.` and `..`).
- Or map the request value to a file name the server chooses (an allow-list or a database id).
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `net/http`
- `encoding/json`
- `os`
- Gin
- Echo
- chi
- gorilla/mux

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A check before the call (`filepath.IsLocal`, `fs.ValidPath`, `strings.Contains(name, "..")`) is
  not recognised: the checked value is still reported.
- `filepath.Base`, `url.QueryEscape` and `url.PathEscape` count as making the value safe, although
  they leave a bare `..` unchanged, which still names the parent directory. `path.Base` does not
  count, since it splits on `/` only.
- `filepath.Clean("/" + name)` is not recognised as making the value safe.
- Request data passed to a function value (a callback) is assumed to reach its result.
- `os.Mkdir`, `os.MkdirAll`, `os.Rename`, `os.Link`, `os.Symlink`, `os.Chmod` and `os.Stat` are not
  checked yet.
- Tests are recognised by a testing parameter of the enclosing function only: a handler declared
  on its own in a test file is still reported.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/go/path/path-traversal.go`](../../../rules/go/path/path-traversal.go) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/go/path/path-traversal.yml`](../../../rules/go/path/path-traversal.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
